skill.displayName: 睿观-图片政策合规监测

llm.summary: This image compliance skill fits its stated purpose, but it needs review because it can publicly upload local images, send extra feedback data, and persist API responses in locations broader than users are told.

dimensions.detail: Calling a LinkFox/Ruiguan image compliance API and using API credentials is coherent with image-based compliance screening, but the local-image upload and feedback-reporting flows add data exposure beyond the core check.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The supplied artifacts describe broad activation for image/violation-database comparisons, automatic Feedback API calls, and a local upload workflow without a clear user-facing consent step before external/public upload.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No artifact-backed evidence shows install-time execution, package-install hooks, or mutation of the agent environment during installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The helper sends environment-derived headers and credentials to a configurable API base URL; external API use is expected, but the endpoint override and header forwarding are broader than necessary without an allowlist or strong disclosure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The script reportedly caches full API responses and may fall back to workspace, home, or temp locations despite documentation promising current-working-directory-only storage; upload_image.py also makes uploaded local files public-read.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending image URLs and possibly local images to LinkFox/Ruiguan services. Avoid using private, confidential, signed, or customer images unless the skill is updated to require explicit upload consent, restrict public exposure, limit cache locations, and document retention and feedback behavior.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: External API calls are expected, but forwarding credential/session headers to a base URL controlled by environment configuration is overbroad for the stated purpose.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Automatic feedback submission is not necessary to perform image compliance checking and creates an additional under-disclosed outbound data flow.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The documented storage boundary and implementation fallback locations appear mismatched, which matters if API responses or image metadata are sensitive.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The trigger language appears broad enough to invoke the external service when user intent is ambiguous.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The local image workflow uploads user files and makes them publicly readable without an explicit warning or confirmation in the supplied instructions.
[SQP-2] expected: Reading API keys from environment variables is a normal integration pattern, but the documentation should add basic secret-handling guidance.
